x: Commentary on Sūrat “Woe to the Defrauders” (al-Muṭaffifīn). In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:

Woe to the defrauders (1) who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full (2) but when they measure or weigh for them, give less (3) Do those not think that they will be resurrected (4) for a Great Day (5) the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds? (6)

The Exalted says: Wayl is the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell, at its lowest part, for those who commit taṭfīf—that is, for those who shortchange people and deprive them of their rights in their measures when they measure for them, or in their scales when they weigh for them, falling short of the full amount due to them. The root of the word is ṭafīf, meaning a small, meagre quantity. The muṭaffif is one who reduces the right-holder’s entitlement below the full and complete amount in measuring or weighing. From this it is said of people
who are equal in reckoning or number: “They are equal, like the ṭaff of the ṣāʿ”—meaning, like a ṣāʿ that is nearly full but falls short of being filled.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about the meaning of this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Abū al-Sāʾib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Ḍirār,
m: , from ʿAbdullāh, that a man said to him: “O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the people of Medina give full measure.” He said: “And what would stop them from giving full measure, when God has said:
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid narrated to us, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
m: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to Medina, they were among the worst of people in measuring, so God revealed:
, and they then improved their measuring

c: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn Khidāsh narrated to me, he said: Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us,
m: the money-changer, from ʿIkrimah, who said: “I bear witness that every measurer and weigher is in the Fire.” He was asked about this, and he said: “None of them weighs as he is weighed, or measures as he is measured, and God has said:

x: who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full

. The Exalted says: Those who, when they take from people the right that is owed to them, take it in full for themselves, so that they measure it from them completely. The particles ʿalā and min alternate in this place, except that when one says “iktaltu minka” it means: “I took my full due from you”
and when they measure for them or weigh for them

. He says: and when they measure for people or weigh for them. It is part of the dialect of the people of the Hijaz to say “wazantuka ḥaqqaka” and “kiltuka ṭaʿāmaka,” meaning “I weighed for you” and “I measured for you.” Whoever takes the speech in this sense makes the pause fall on “hum,” and makes (hum) stand in the accusative position. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, as is reported of him, treats them as two separate words, pausing at “kālū” and at “wazanū,” and then beginning anew: “hum yukhsirūn”

. Whoever takes the speech in this sense makes “hum” nominative, and treats “kālū” and “wazanū” as complete in themselves. In my view the correct position is to pause at “hum,” because if “kālū” and “wazanū” [were complete in themselves], with “hum” a new sentence, then “kālū” and “wazanū” would be written with an alif separating each of them from (hum), since that is how the written text proceeds in comparable cases when no object pronoun is attached to the verb. Their writing it in this place without an alif is therefore the clearest evidence that “hum” is simply the pronoun standing for those who are measured or weighed for. So the meaning of the verse, the matter being as we have described, is as we have explained
Do those not think that they will be resurrected (4) for a Great Day

. The Exalted says: Do these defrauders of people in their measures and scales not think that they will be raised up from their graves after their death for a Day of tremendous consequence, terrible in its affair, dreadful in its horror?
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. “The Day when they stand” is an explanation of the Day first, the one in the genitive; but since the preposition lām was not repeated with it, it is referred back to

, as if He had said: Do those not think that they will be resurrected on the Day when mankind will stand? Its being put in the accusative is also permissible, with the sense of the genitive, because the annexation is not a pure one; and if it were put in the genitive in apposition to the first Day, that would not be a solecism; and if it were put in the nominative, that too would be permissible, as the poet said

: “I was like one with two legs—one leg sound, and one on which Time cast its blow, so it withered.” It is related that people will stand before the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat bridles them; some say the length of that standing is three hundred years, and others say forty years.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd al-Kindī narrated to me, he said: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet,
m: peace and blessings be upon him, concerning His saying:
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: “One of you will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears”

c: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet,
m: peace and blessings be upon him:
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: “One of them will be submerged in his sweat up to the middle of his ears”

c: Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, who said: Ibn ʿUmar said:
m: the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
—until one of them stands in his sweat up to the middle of his ears.

c: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “On the Day of Resurrection people will be made to stand, in reverence for the greatness of God, until the sweat bridles them up to the middle of their ears”

c: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
—on the Day of Resurrection, in reverence for the greatness of the Most Merciful.” Then he mentioned the like of it (1).

c: Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī narrated to us, he said: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, recited this verse: “
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
.” He said: “They will stand until the sweat reaches the middle of their ears”

c: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, he said: Nāfiʿ narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said
: “People will stand before the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection until one of them is submerged up to the middle of his ears in his sweat”

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from Ibn ʿUmar,
m: the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: They will stand for a hundred years

c: Tamīm ibn al-Muntaṣir narrated to us, he said: Yazīd informed us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say
: “People will stand before the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat bridles a man up to the middle of his ears”

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet,
m: peace and blessings be upon him, to the same effect.

c: Ibn al-Muthannā and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us,
m: both saying: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbaydullāh

, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “People will stand before the Lord of the worlds until one of them stands in his sweat up to the middle of his ears”
, known as Ibn Ṣudrān, narrated to me, he said:

c: Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Salām ibn ʿAjlān narrated to us, he said:
m: Yazīd al-Madanī narrated to us, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Bashīr al-Ghifārī: “How will you fare on a Day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds for three hundred years of the days of this world, with no word coming to them from heaven and no command being given to them?” Bashīr said: “God is the One whose help is sought
, O Messenger of God.” He said: “When you retire to your bed, seek refuge with God from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and from the evil of the reckoning”

c: Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah al-Yarbūʿī narrated to me, he said: Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd,
m: the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds

. He said: They will remain forty years with their heads raised toward the sky, no one speaking to them, the sweat having bridled every righteous and every wicked person. He said: Then a caller will call out: “Is it not just on the part of your Lord that He created you, then fashioned you, then provided for you, and then you turned to another besides Him, that He should hand over each of you to whomever you turned to in the world?” They will say: “Yes.” Then he related the hadith at length

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Qays ibn Sakan, who said:
m: ʿAbdullāh related while he was with ʿUmar:
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds

. He said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot and naked, bridled by the sweat, with no human being speaking to them for forty years. Then he related something similar

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: It was mentioned to us that Kaʿb used to say: They will stand for three hundred years

c: [Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Mihrān narrated to us,
m: the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: Kaʿb used to say: They will stand for the length of three hundred years]

. Qatādah said: And al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād al-ʿAdawī narrated to us, he said: It has reached me that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believer until it is like one of his obligatory prayers. He said: Mihrān narrated to us, he said:

c: al-ʿUmarī narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say:
the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds
. He said: “A man will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears”

c: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: People will stand before the Lord of the worlds until one of them stands in his sweat up to the middle of his ears
. Yaʿqūb said: Ismāʿīl said: I said to Ibn ʿAwn: “Did he mention the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in this hadith?” He said: “Yes, God willing.”

c: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: My uncle narrated to me, he said: Mālik ibn Anas informed me, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar,
m: that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “People will stand before the Lord of the worlds until one of them is submerged in his sweat up to half of his ears”

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn (7) And what will make you know what Sijjīn is? (8) A written record (9) Woe that Day to the deniers (10) who deny the Day of Judgment (11)

The Exalted says: “No!”—that is, the matter is not as these disbelievers suppose, that they will not be resurrected and will not be punished. Indeed their record, in which are written the deeds they used to do in the world, is

, which is the lowest, seventh earth. It is of the pattern fiʿʿīl, from sijn (prison), just as one says sikkīr (a habitual drunkard) from sukr (drunkenness), and fissīq (a habitual sinner) from fisq (sinfulness).
The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of this; some of them said what we have said.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Mughīth ibn Sumayy:
m: Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: In the seventh earth.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Mughīth ibn Sumayy, who said:
m: Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: The lowest earth. He said: Iblīs is bound with iron and chains in the lowest earth

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim informed me, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Hilāl ibn Yisāf, who said:
m: We were sitting with Kaʿb—I, Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, Khālid ibn ʿArʿarah, and a group of our companions—when Ibn ʿAbbās came and sat beside Kaʿb, and said: “O Kaʿb, tell me about
.” Kaʿb said: “As for Sijjīn, it is the lowest, seventh earth, and in it are the souls of the disbelievers, beneath the cheek of Iblīs”

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
: It is mentioned that ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr used to say: It is the lowest earth; in it are the souls of the disbelievers, and their deeds are evil deeds

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah:
m: . He said: In the bottom of the seventh earth

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He says: Their deeds are in a record in the lowest earth

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the saying of God:
. He said: Their deeds are in the seventh earth and do not ascend
. al-Ḥārith narrated to me, he said:

c: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid,
ʿUmar ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Mujālid narrated to me, he said:
m: Muṭarrif ibn Māzin, judge of Yemen, narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said:
is the seventh earth. I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His saying:
. He says: In the lowest earth

c: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: Abū Hilāl narrated to us, he said: Qatādah narrated to us,
m: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: The seventh, lowest earth.

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying:
No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: It is said that Sijjīn is the lowest earth, and that Sijjīn is in the nearest heaven.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the cheek
Mention of those who said so:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī narrated to us, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ḥumayd, from Shimr, who said:
m: Ibn ʿAbbās came to Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, and Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: “Tell me about the saying of God:
Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
” (the verse). Kaʿb said: “The soul of the wicked person

is taken up toward heaven, but heaven refuses to receive it; it is then sent down toward the earth, but the earth refuses to receive it. So it descends and enters beneath the seven earths until it is brought to Sijjīn, which is the cheek of Iblīs. Then from Sijjīn, from beneath the cheek of Iblīs, a parchment is brought out for it, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the cheek of Iblīs—with its knowing destruction—until the Day of Resurrection”

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd,
m: Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: Beneath the cheek of Iblīs

x: Others said: It is an open pit in Hell. They related a report about this from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.

c: Isḥāq ibn Wahb al-Wāsiṭī narrated it to us, he said: Masʿūd ibn Mūsā ibn Mushkān al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, he said:
m: ibn Khuzaymah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, from Shuʿayb ibn Ṣafwān, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell, whereas Sijjīn is open”
b.via: Masʿūd ibn Mūsā ibn Mushkān al-Wāsiṭī

x: Some of the people of Arabic
said: They mention that “Sijjīn” is the rock beneath the earth. He said: We think

that “Sijjīn” is one of its attributes, because if it were its name it would not be made fully inflected (nunated). He said: And if you say, “I made it fully inflected because I took ‘the rock’ to mean the stone in which the record is,” that would be a valid way of taking it.
As for why I chose the view I chose regarding the meaning of His saying

c: it is because Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said:
m: narrated to us, from Zādhān Abū ʿAmr, from al-Barāʾ, who said:

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl, from Zādhān, from al-Barāʾ,
m: that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, speaking of the soul of the wicked person and how it is taken up toward heaven, said: “They take it up, and they pass with it by no company of angels without their saying: ‘What is this foul soul?’ They say: ‘So-and-so,’ using the ugliest of the names by which he was called in the world, until they reach the nearest heaven with it and ask for it to be opened, but it is not opened for him.” Then the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, recited: “
The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle
[al-Aʿrāf: 40]. Then God says: ‘Write his record in the lowest part of the earth, in Sijjīn, in the lowest earth’”

c: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, from Mujāhid,
m: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn
. He said: Sijjīn is a rock in the seventh earth, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it

x: And what will make you know what Sijjīn is?

. The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And what will make you know, O Muḥammad, what that record is? Then the Exalted explained it, saying: it is a written record. By “marqūm” He means “written.”
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: . He said: A record that is written

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah:
m: And what will make you know what Sijjīn is? (8) A written record
. He said: Evil has been inscribed for them

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying:

x: Woe that Day to the deniers
. The Exalted says: Woe on that Day to those who deny these signs,
who deny the Day of Judgment
. He says: those who deny the Day of reckoning and recompense.

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying:
who deny the Day of Judgment
. He said: The people of polytheism deny the Judgment. And he recited:
And those who disbelieved said, “Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you…”
[Sabaʾ: 7] to the end of the verse.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
And none denies it except every sinful transgressor (12) When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Legends of the ancients” (13) No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts (14)
The Exalted says: None denies the Day of Judgment except every transgressor who has transgressed against God in what he says, opposing His command, sinful toward his Lord.

c: As Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah:
m: Woe that Day to the deniers (10)
And none denies it except every sinful transgressor
—that is, [denies] the Day of Judgment—except every transgressor in his speech, sinful toward his Lord
When Our verses are recited to him
. The Exalted says: when Our proofs and evidences, which We have made clear in Our Book that We sent down to Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, are read to him,
He says: he says: this is what the ancients set down in lines and wrote, of tales and reports.

x: No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts
. The Exalted says, denying them in their saying that: No, it is not so; rather, it has

. He says: it has overcome their hearts and submerged them, and sins have encompassed them and veiled them. It is said: “rānat al-khamru ʿalā ʿaqlihi,” “the wine overcame his mind,” and it “tarīnu ʿalayhi raynan.” That is when he becomes drunk and it overpowers his mind. Among this is the saying of Abū Zubayd al-Ṭāʾī

: “Then when he saw him, the wine overcame him—while you do not overcome him through caution.” By “tarīnuhu” he means “you overpower him with fear.” He says: he is intoxicated and does not awaken. And among this is the saying of the rajaz poet
: “We were not quenched until she set out at midday, and I was overcome, and the cupbearer who passed the evening with me was overcome.”
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this, and a report to this effect has come from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abū Khālid narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is dotted on his heart. If he repents, it is polished away from him; if he returns, it returns until it grows great in his heart. That is the rān that God mentioned:

The Arabs do the same with every plural that has no singular or dual form built from it: they pluralize it with nūn, for females and males alike, as we have explained; and from that is their saying for men and women: “ʿishrūn” (twenty) and “thalāthūn” (thirty)

. He said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father, from Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ, from Zayd

m: . He said: Its end is musk; some are given it mixed with camphor and sealed with musk

Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah narrated to us, from Jābir,
m: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ, from Abū al-Dardāʾ:

x: Mention of those who said so:

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us,

. He said: Its clay is musk

m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying:
: its seal with God is musk, whereas its seal today in this world is clay
. The most correct of the views on this in our view is the view of those who said: the meaning is: its end and its outcome is musk—that is, it
is sweet-smelling, and its scent at the end of their drinking is sealed

for them with the scent of musk. We say that this is the most correct view because the word “seal” has no sense in Arabic speech other than sealing and finishing, as in their saying “So-and-so sealed the Qurʾān” when he reached its end. So since there is no intelligible sense of sealing with clay for the drink of the people of Paradise—their drink flowing like water in rivers, not aged in jars so that they would be plastered with clay and sealed—it is known

that the sound view is the other: that it is the outcome, the last thing drunk, which is that with which the drink is concluded. As for “sealing” in the sense of mixing, we do not know it to be attested in Arabic speech. The reciters also differed in how they read this. The generality of the reciters of the regions read
except al-Kisāʾī, who used to read it (khātamuhu miskun)
. The correct view in our opinion is what the reciters of the regions hold, namely

, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. Khitām and khātam, though they differ in form, are close in meaning, except that khātam is a noun and khitām is a verbal noun; and from this is the saying of al-Farazdaq
: “They spent the night at my two sides, laid low, and I spent the night breaking the locks of the seal.” A parallel to this is their saying: “He is of noble ṭābiʿ

The generality of the reciters of the regions read {khitāmuhu miskun} except al-Kisāʾī, who used to read it (khātamuhu miskun) (1).
The correct view in our opinion is what the reciters of the regions hold, namely {khitāmuhu} (2), because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: and for that let the competitors compete

. The Exalted says: In this bliss which He, glorified be His praise, has described as given to these righteous on the Day of Resurrection, let the competitors compete. Tanāfus (competition) is when a man envies another for something he has and wishes it to be his rather than the other’s; it is derived from the nafīs, the precious thing, that which people’s souls long for, seek, and desire. The sense here is as though: let people strive for it, race toward it in seeking it, and let their souls be eager for it.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
and its mixture is from Tasnīm (27) a spring from which those brought near drink (28) Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed (29)
The Exalted says: The mixture of this raḥīq is from tasnīm. Tasnīm is of the form tafʿīl, from the saying of one who says: “sannamtu

tasnīman,” when you make it flow over them from above them. So its meaning in this place is: its mixture is of water that comes down upon them from above and flows down over them. Mujāhid and al-Kalbī both said this.

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying:
. He said: A tasnīm that rises on high

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī,
m: . He said: A tasnīm that pours down over them from above them, and it is the drink of those brought near
. The rest of the people of interpretation said: It is a spring with which the raḥīq is mixed for the Companions of the Right, whereas those brought near drink it unmixed.

x: Mention of those who said so:

c: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbdullāh,
m: . He said: A spring in Paradise which those brought near drink
, and which is mixed for the Companions of the Right

c: Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq, from ʿAbdullāh:
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: Those brought near drink it unmixed, and it is mixed for the Companions of the Right.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith, from Masrūq:
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm

. He said: A spring in Paradise which those brought near drink unmixed, and which is mixed for the Companions of the Right. He said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Murrah, from Masrūq:
a spring from which those brought near drink
. He said: Those brought near drink from it unmixed, and it is mixed for the Companions of the Right.

c: Ṭalḥah ibn Yaḥyā al-Yarbūʿī narrated to me, he said: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: In Paradise there is a spring from which those brought near drink unmixed, and which is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
from which those brought near drink unmixed, and in which a mixture is made for those below them

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥārith,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: Tasnīm is a spring in Paradise which those brought near drink unmixed, and which is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, he said: Abū Ḥamzah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: A spring from which those brought near drink, and in which a mixture is made for those below them

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm (27) a spring from which those brought near drink
: a spring [of those that are in]
Paradise with which the wine is mixed.

c: Yaʿqūb narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: Hidden delights that God has concealed for the people of Paradise

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, from Abū Ṣāliḥ,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
. He said: It is the noblest drink in Paradise; for those brought near it is unmixed, and for the people of Paradise it is a mixture

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: and its mixture is from Tasnīm
: a noble drink; a spring in Paradise which those brought near drink unmixed, and which is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying:
from Tasnīm (27) a spring from which those brought near drink
. He said: It has reached us that it is a spring that comes out from beneath the Throne, and it is the mixture of this wine—that is, the mixture of the raḥīq
. I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His saying:
: a drink whose name is Tasnīm, and it is among the noblest of drinks

. So the meaning of the verse is: the mixture of the raḥīq is from a spring that is made to flow from above them and pours down over them, from which those brought near to God drink unmixed, and which is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.

x: The people of Arabic differed over the reason for the accusative in His saying

(a spring). One of the grammarians of Basra said: If you wish, you may make its accusative rest on “they are given to drink a spring,” and if you wish you may make it a praise-construction, cut off from the beginning of the sentence, as if you were saying: “I mean a spring.” One of the grammarians of Kufa
said: The accusative of ʿayn has two explanations. One: that one intends “from the tasnīm of a spring,” so that when the tanwīn is added it becomes accusative, as He said:
or feeding, on a day of hunger (14), an orphan
Have We not made the earth a receptacle (25) for the living
[al-Mursalāt: 25–26]. The other explanation: that one intends “from water that was made to flow from above, a spring,” as in your saying “he raised up a spring from which one drinks.”
He said: If tasnīm is not a name for the water, then ʿayn is indefinite and tasnīm is definite; and if it is a name for the water, then ʿayn is definite
, so it came out accusative. Another of the Basrans said:
, and it came indefinite, so you put it in the accusative as a descriptive qualifier of it

. And another said: It is accusative in the sense of “from water that rises on high as a spring.” The correct view in our opinion is that tasnīm is a definite noun and ʿayn is indefinite, and it is accusative for that reason, since it is a description of it. We say that this is correct because of what we have previously related from the people of interpretation, that Tasnīm is the spring itself; so it is known from this that since ʿayn is accusative and indefinite, Tasnīm is definite.
Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed
. The Exalted says: Those who earned sins and disbelieved in God in the world used to laugh, in it, at those who affirmed the oneness of God and believed in Him, in mockery of them.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed
: in the world, they would say: “By God, these people are liars, and they have nothing to stand on”—in mockery of them

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:

And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks (30) And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting (2) (31) And when they saw them, they would say, “Indeed, those are lost” (32) But they had not been sent as guardians over them (33)
The Exalted says: These who committed crimes, whenever the believers passed by them, would

. He says: they would wink at one another about the believer, in mockery and ridicule of him. And His saying: (And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting). He says: these criminals, when they went back to their families from their gatherings, would go back delighted and self-admiring.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: ʿAlī narrated to me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: (they would return jesting). He said: self-admiring.

c: Yūnus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: (And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting). He said: He returned delighting in luxury. He said: This is in the world; then the Fire follows it in the Hereafter.

x: Some of the scholars of the Arabs’ speech used to distinguish between the meanings of fākihīn and fakihīn: he would say that fākihīn means enjoying comforts, and fakihīn means exuberant. Another would say
: they are one and the same in meaning, and it is simply like ṭāmiʿ and ṭamiʿ, bākhil and bakhil.
And when they saw them, they would say, “Indeed, those are lost”
. The Exalted says: And when the criminals saw the believers, they said to them: “Indeed, these are lost, astray from the highway of truth and the path of rectitude,”
But they had not been sent as guardians over them
. He, glorified be His praise, says: These disbelievers who said to the believers “these are lost” were not sent as guardians over them, watching over their deeds
. He says: they were only charged with belief in God and acting in obedience to Him, and were not made overseers of others, keeping watch over their deeds and scrutinizing them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers (34) on adorned couches, observing (35) Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do? (36)
—and that is the Day of Resurrection—
. He says: on their couches that are in canopies, they are looking at them while they are in Paradise and the disbelievers are in the Fire being punished.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers (34) on adorned couches, observing
. He said: He means the raised couches over which are canopies. Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The wall between Paradise and the Fire will have doors opened in it

for them, and the believers will look at the people of the Fire while the believers are upon the couches, looking at how they are being punished, and they will laugh at them; and that will be among the things by which God delights their eyes: seeing how God takes vengeance on them

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah,
m: So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers
: It was mentioned to us that Kaʿb used to say: Between Paradise and the Fire there are windows, and when the believer wants to look at an enemy he had in the world, he looks out
through one of those windows. God, glorified be His praise, said:
and he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blaze
[al-Ṣāffāt: 55]—that is, in the middle of the Fire; and it was mentioned to us that he saw the skulls of the people boiling

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah: Kaʿb said:
m: Between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire there are windows; no man among the people of Paradise wishes to look at another of the people of the Fire without doing so

c: It was related to me, from al-Ḥusayn, who said:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His saying:
So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers (34) on adorned couches, observing

: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: The wall is between the people of Paradise and the Fire, and doors are opened for the people of Paradise, and they look, while on the couches, at the people of the Fire, seeing how they are punished, and they laugh at them; and this is among the things by which God delights their eyes, that they look at their enemy and see how God takes vengeance on them.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān:
m: So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers

. He said: The disbelievers are brought until they look at the people of Paradise in Paradise, on couches, and when they look at them, the doors are shut in their faces, and the people of Paradise laugh at them. That is His saying:
So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers (34) on adorned couches, observing

x: Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?

. The Exalted says: Have the disbelievers been repaid and recompensed for what they used to do in the world to the believers, of their mockery of them and their laughing at them—by the believers’ laughing at them in the Hereafter, while the believers are on the couches looking, and they are in the Fire being punished? And
is of the form fuʿʿila, from thawāb (reward) and jazāʾ (recompense); one says of it: “thawwaba so-and-so so-and-so for his deed,” and “athābahu” for it.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said so:

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, he said: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān:
m: Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do
—when they used to mock? End of the commentary on Sūrat “Woe to the Defrauders”.
